nodes.label: integration-brokers workflow
nodes.rationale: Phase B of the test-coverage audit: each suite brings up a real broker in Docker and runs scenarios against the live socket. Matrix-parallel so wall clock is the slowest suite (Kafka, ~30 s) rather than the sum of all of them. Trigger shape mirrors the cluster integration.yml, with the nightly cron at 03:30 UTC offset from its 03:00 so the two do not fight for the same runner pool.

nodes.label: Live broker matrix
nodes.rationale: Sixteen legs: MinIO, Mosquitto, Redpanda, RabbitMQ, NATS, Redis Streams, gRPC echo, k3s, PostgreSQL, MariaDB, libSQL (sqld), SQL Server 2022, MongoDB, DynamoDB Local, plus CockroachDB and YugabyteDB as Postgres-wire certifications of the existing stores rather than new backends (#401). Each entry carries dir, the test:integration:<npm> script name (redis-streams uses the short redis name) and a display image. fail-fast: false so one broker regression does not mask the others, and the nightly run catches upstream :latest image regressions - each suite tracking :latest is the point.

nodes.label: Container log capture on failure
nodes.rationale: On failure every container's stdout/stderr is dumped so a flaky scenario is debuggable from the workflow log alone rather than by re-running locally and praying for a repro; teardown runs with always(). --exit-code-from runner propagates the in-container status so a failing scenario turns the step red.
